name: Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Ltd (GRSE)
tagline: Debt-free defence-PSU shipyard with 43% ROCE, freshly-minted Navratna status, and a Rs 33,000+ Cr Next-Generation Corvette award now CCS-cleared and awaiting signature - best-in-batch fundamentals, but already large-cap by size
business_overview: GRSE is a Kolkata-based defence PSU shipyard supplying the Indian Navy and Coast Guard, with a growing non-defence shipbuilding order share (25% of order book now, up from 2% five years ago). Recent execution highlights include anti-submarine shallow watercraft (4 of 8 delivered ahead of schedule) and P17 Alpha frigates (2 of 3 delivered ahead of schedule).
fundamentals_table: Rs 7,002 Cr FY26 (+38% YoY); Q1 FY27 Rs 1,815 Cr (+39% YoY)
Rs 748 Cr FY26 (+42% YoY); Q1 FY27 Rs 173 Cr (+44% YoY)
Rs 13,596 Cr (Jun-2026; 44 platforms/11 projects) - a pending Rs 33,000-36,000 Cr Next-Gen Corvette award (CCS-approved, signing expected Q2 FY27) would roughly treble it
P/E 34.5x, P/B 10.5x (18-Sep-2026) - already prices in continued high-30s% growth
fundamentals_narrative: Exceptional capital efficiency (43% ROCE, 31.8% ROE) on a near debt-free balance sheet, with genuine execution behind it - FY26 revenue grew 38% to Rs7,002 Cr and PAT 42% to Rs748 Cr on a record 8 warship deliveries, and Q1 FY27 continued at the same high-30s% pace (revenue +39%, PAT +44%). GRSE was elevated to Navratna status in June 2026 (29th CPSE to achieve it), giving it materially greater capex/investment autonomy. The order book itself fell to Rs13,596 Cr (Jun-2026, first time below Rs15,000 Cr in a decade) - management frames this as fast execution rather than weak demand, and the framing is credible given the pipeline: a ~Rs33,000-36,000 Cr Next-Generation Corvette (NGC) award for 5 stealth corvettes has Cabinet Committee on Security approval and finalised commercial/technical terms, with formal signing expected in Q2 FY27 - though that is itself a ~2-quarter slip from the originally guided March-2026 signing (when management had targeted an ~Rs50,000 Cr order book by FY26-end). Revenue from NGC only starts H2 FY28, with meaningful contribution from FY29. The catch, as before, is size: at ~Rs27,628 Cr market cap and 34.5x trailing P/E / 10.5x P/B, this is already a large-cap trading on a full multiple, not a re-rating candidate.
technical_read: Not independently pulled this pass; 52-week range Rs1,964-3,339, price ~Rs2,412 as of 18-Sep-2026 - mid-range, off the highs after the order-book-fall headline earlier in 2026.

bse_notes: No red-flag corporate actions found. Promoter (Government of India / Ministry of Defence) holding stable at 74.50%, no pledge.
bull_case: 43% ROCE / 31.8% ROE on a near debt-free balance sheet, with FY26 revenue +38% and PAT +42% backed by real execution (record 8 warship deliveries, several ahead of schedule)
Elevated to Navratna status in June 2026 (29th CPSE) - materially greater capex/investment autonomy just as the order pipeline is about to step up

Next-Generation Corvette award (~Rs33,000-36,000 Cr, 5 stealth corvettes) is CCS-approved with commercial/technical terms finalised - effectively a near-certain, not speculative, forward order, expected to formally sign in Q2 FY27

Diversifying book: non-defence/export share up from 2% to 25% of order book over five years, including a 12-vessel hybrid-propulsion Multi-Purpose Vessel export program for a German client (largest commercial export order to date)
India's naval/Atmanirbharta shipbuilding push is a genuine, multi-year structural tailwind, and GRSE is one of only a handful of yards qualified for frontline warship construction
bear_case: At ~Rs27,628 Cr and already large-cap, a 10x-in-2-3-years or 100x-in-10-years move is not mathematically plausible regardless of execution quality - the same size ceiling that applies to Force Motors applies here
Valuation is already full: 34.5x trailing P/E and 10.5x P/B price in continued high-30s% growth even before the NGC step-up, which does not contribute revenue until H2 FY28-FY29

Management's own order-book guidance has already slipped once - a ~Rs50,000 Cr order book was targeted by FY26-end contingent on NGC signing by March 2026; NGC signing has since moved to Q2 FY27, a ~2-quarter delay on a single-point-of-failure commitment
Debtor days rose from 34 to 63.6 and reported PAT includes ~Rs301 Cr of other income - both are earnings-quality watch items, not yet red flags
PSU order timing and government budget/approval cycles (illustrated by the NGC delay itself) introduce lumpiness that isn't fully visible yet in this very young ValuePickr thread
Vivek_6954's trusted-thread post shows partial profit-booking rather than a sustained top-holding stance, a milder trusted signal than a very-high case
verdict_headline: Best-in-batch fundamentals plus a near-certain Rs33,000+ Cr order make this an elite PSU compounder - but size alone caps thesis_fit, and it's already a High-conviction 'Overall' name, not a 10x/100x one
verdict_reasoning: 43% ROCE, 31.8% ROE, near debt-free, and Navratna status place GRSE among the strongest fundamentals profiles in this project regardless of size

The Next-Generation Corvette award is now CCS-approved with terms finalised - a thesis-critical forward commitment that has de-risked considerably since the last pass, even though its own signing timeline has already slipped once

At ~Rs27,628 Cr market cap and 34.5x P/E, GRSE has already crossed into large-cap territory and the multiple already prices in continued high growth - the same size math that rules out Force Motors applies here, so thesis_fit stays neither on size grounds regardless of the strong four_box inputs (tailwind yes, moat yes)
Given the quality and de-risked forward pipeline, this is upgraded to High conviction as an 'Overall' confidence-list name even though it cannot qualify for the project's 10x/100x thesis_fit labels
Not flagged for 30-day revisit given thesis_fit is 'neither' on size grounds and no near-term catalyst changes that math

four_box.note: Naval/Atmanirbharta shipbuilding is a real structural tailwind, reinforced by the NGC award, the ONGC order, and export diversification. PSU-shipyard positioning (Navratna status, one of a handful of Navy-qualified yards, 43% ROCE, ahead-of-schedule execution) is a genuine moat. Explicit size math (~Rs27,628cr, already large-cap) rules out tam regardless of pipeline strength. Valuation is weak, not yes - 34.5x P/E / 10.5x P/B already price in continued high growth. Score 2.5 stays below the 3.0 threshold; the large-cap protocol means no written exception is available here, so thesis_fit remains neither even though this is a legitimate High-conviction 'Overall' name.

quality_metrics.note: Debt is negligible (~Rs37 Cr, Mar-2026) against FY26 EBITDA in the Rs1,000+ Cr range, so net_debt_to_ebitda is effectively net-cash/immaterial, but the precise net-cash figure (shipyards carry large customer-advance balances) was not cleanly sourced this pass, so left null rather than guessed. Quarterly EBITDA margin has been lumpy (screener-reported ~9% in three of the last four quarters, spiking to ~17% in Q4 FY26) given milestone-based revenue recognition - classified 'expanding' on the recent trend but flagged as partly mix/timing-driven in earnings_quality below. fcf_conversion_pct not sourced this pass - working capital in shipbuilding is heavily advance-funded and CFO/capex figures were not cleanly separable from open sources within budget.
